findings.reason: the fallback exists precisely to close the gap the prior review raised (a row whose only dispatched-head source is its node id has no `.at-` path, so it is listed by §2 yet refused by §3), and a worker following the plan literally receives a run id where a head is required, so the node-id-only rows — including §2's own known-correct row read through the node-id suffix — stay refused rather than corrected; the plan must name the head-extracting step, not a helper that returns the source.
findings.text: §3's new head fallback says the verb reads "the hex suffix of the node id through `round_node_source`" (`reckon/crew/repair.py:310`), but `round_node_source(node_id, prefix)` is the inverse of `round_node_id`: it strips the review prefix and the trailing `-<head[:12]>` suffix and returns the *source* (the reviewed run id), discarding exactly the head the sentence says it yields; the correct route is the census's own `_node_head_suffix` (`scripts/review_rows_with_another_rounds_verdict.py:59`), which recovers `raw[len(source) + 1:]`.

rubric_items.done_when: pass — §3's five done-when items are measurable and item 4 names a declared negative control (the new test file's reader cases FAILED by id at the base revision, logged under the run directory), with the red-first framing repeated on the "Negative control" line.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the verb writes the row's committed per-run file under docs/state/<project>/runs/ and the gate log lands under the run directory; no scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `supersede-review`, `review_correction` and the unnamed accessor carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and describe the mechanism rather than the history.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3's newly added node-id fallback names `round_node_source` as reading "the hex suffix of the node id", but that function returns the source (run id), not the head, so the fallback the section added is unfollowable as written.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3's two bullets (one reader accessor, one append verb) are the two halves of one deliverable, a correction every reader honours; neither is closable on its own, so the node still closes on one verdict.
